title: Event Versioning
description: Learn strategies for evolving event schemas over time without breaking existing consumers or historical replay.

data.text: Events are immutable, but your code is not. Eventually you will need to change the shape of an event type. Maybe you add a field, rename a property, or split one event into two. Because old events remain in the store forever, your consumers must be able to read both old and new versions. Event versioning is the discipline of evolving event schemas safely.

The safest strategy is backward-compatible evolution: add optional fields, never remove required ones, and avoid renaming. If you must make a breaking change, create a new event type with a new name, such as `OrderShippedV2`. Old consumers continue handling `OrderShipped` while new consumers handle `OrderShippedV2`. This doubles the work temporarily but keeps the system running.

rows: Most common; new fields have defaults
Phased field removal over multiple releases
Breaking changes that cannot be avoided

data.text: When reading events, detect the version and transform the payload into the current schema. A version number or distinct event type name tells the consumer which contract to use.

data.title: Version-Aware Event Handler in C#
data.content: Handle both OrderShipped and OrderShippedV2 events in the same projection.

data.text: For small event stores, you can rewrite old events into the new schema. This is called inline migration or upcasting. You replay all events through a transform function that converts V1 payloads to V2 and writes them back. After the migration, all consumers see only the new schema. This is risky for large stores and requires downtime or dual-write during the transition.

data.caption: Event versioning strategies: compatible evolution vs. new event type
data.definition:
flowchart TD
    A[Need to Change Schema] --> B{Breaking Change?}
    B -->|No| C[Add Optional Field]
    B -->|Yes| D{Store Size Small?}
    D -->|Yes| E[Inline Rewrite]
    D -->|No| F[New Event Type V2]
    C --> G[Single Consumer Handles Both]
    F --> H[Old Consumer Handles V1
    New Consumer Handles V2]
    E --> I[All Events in New Schema]

data.title: Never Edit Existing Events
data.text: Overwriting an event in place breaks the event log and invalidates any projections built from the original. Always append new events or migrate by rewriting streams in a controlled process.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Prefer backward-compatible changes: add optional fields, never remove required ones.
Use a new event type name (V2) for breaking changes.
Version-aware consumers can read both old and new event shapes.
Inline rewrites are possible but risky for large event stores.
data.takeaway: Events are forever; design schemas that can evolve without breaking the past.
